    AI Mode reply for chromedp set user data dir

    To set a custom user data directory in chromedp, use the chromedp.UserDataDir function inside a custom chromedp.NewExecAllocator context. By default, chromedp creates a temporary directory and destroys it when the browser exits. Providing a persistent directory lets you preserve cookies, login sessions, and local history. 
    Code Example
    go
    package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/chromedp/chromedp"
)

func main() {
	// 1. Combine default options with your custom user data directory
	opts := append(chromedp.DefaultExecAllocatorOptions[:],
		chromedp.UserDataDir("/path/to/your/custom/user-data"), // Overrides the temporary directory
		chromedp.Flag("headless", false),                      // Optional: visible browser to verify profile data
	)

	// 2. Create the allocator context with your options
	allocCtx, allocCancel := chromedp.NewExecAllocator(context.Background(), opts...)
	defer allocCancel()

	// 3. Create the operational chromedp context
	ctx, cancel := chromedp.NewContext(allocCtx)
	defer cancel()

	// 4. Run your tasks
	var title string
	err := chromedp.Run(ctx,
		chromedp.Navigate("https://example.com"),
		chromedp.Title(&title),
	)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("Failed running task: %v", err)
	}

	log.Printf("Page Title: %s", title)

	// 5. Explicitly cancel operational context or call allocCancel() to let Chrome cleanly flush profile changes
	cancel() 
}
    Use code with caution.
    Critical Rules & Edge Cases
    • Graceful Shutdown: You must ensure your context cancel functions or chromedp.Cancel are executed at shutdown. If the Go application crashes or exits forcefully, Chrome will not flush data or sessions to the disk directory completely. 
    • Single Instance Limit: Chrome only allows one running instance per user data directory at any given time. If you try to spin up multiple parallel chromedp allocators pointing to the exact same folder path, the execution will fail or lock up. 
    • Profile Multi-Tenancy: If your specified folder contains multiple sub-profiles, you can pair the UserDataDir call with a profile flag to load a specific account:
      go
      chromedp.UserDataDir("/path/to/Chrome/User Data"),
chromedp.Flag("profile-directory", "Profile 1"),
      Use code with caution.
       
    If you are running into issues, tell me: Are you getting a directory locked error, or are your cookies/sessions failing to save between script runs?
